CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a variable response to the current therapeutic regimen. He indicates that his sleep quality has remained stable, averaging approximately 8 hours per night. However, he continues to struggle with sleep onset, particularly before workdays characterized by higher stress levels. The trazodone at 75 mg seems to help with nocturnal awakenings, but he continues to report frequent early morning awakenings, which contribute to feelings of fatigue upon waking.
In regard to persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith notes some improvement, citing a slight increase in energy levels during the day, which he attributes to his ongoing commitment to mindfulness and yoga practices. Nevertheless, he still experiences significant fatigue, particularly during high-pressure work periods. He describes this fatigue as both physically and mentally exhausting. His headache symptoms remain a concern; he reports experiencing headaches 2-3 times per week with intensities ranging from 4-7 out of 10. He has been using ibuprofen 400 mg for relief, approximately 3-4 times weekly, but expresses apprehension about the potential long-term use of this medication.
Mr. Smith continues to adhere to his holistic treatment plan, including regular acupuncture sessions and yoga classes, which he finds beneficial. His participation in cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions continues, and he reports that these sessions have been instrumental in managing anxiety, particularly concerning work-related stressors. He expresses a desire to enhance his coping mechanisms further.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (usage stable) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 25 mg daily (titration to be considered) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where project deadlines remain a significant source of stress. He remains active in yoga and meditation, which he finds helpful for managing stress. He abstains from alcohol and maintains a primarily plant-based diet, although he admits to occasional consumption of processed foods during particularly stressful periods.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety remains stable with some noted improvements; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency remains stable; intensity fluctuates; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.7F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Encourage ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions to further develop coping strategies for work-related stress. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; revisit sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset difficulties persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the stable headache frequency and intensity, continue topiramate at 25 mg daily, with plans to reassess in the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices. Refer to a nutritionist for dietary optimization during high-stress periods. Consider exploring additional therapeutic options if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-10-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
